I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it fits my irrigation condition, and it spreads my risk better than pushing too much land into vegetables. I have 25 years in the field, so I do not chase fancy changes. I will put 200 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 32.9 mu for cauliflower because it gives me cash income, but I do not want too much vegetable area because it takes more labor, fertilizer, water, and pesticide management. With a 3-person household, I need a plan I can actually finish on time, so I will use improved seed in wheat, hybrid seed in maize, and improved cauliflower seed. I will use moderate fertilizer rates, rely on well irrigation where it matters, plough for wheat and cauliflower to make a good seedbed, and use no-tillage for maize after wheat to save time and hold moisture. I am aiming for steady yield, not the highest possible yield, because a stable crop is better for me than taking big input risks.
